confirmation.summary: Abnormal copper metabolism, corneal Kayser-Fleischer rings and ATP7B variants.
evidence: Based on results showing abnormal copper metabolism, corneal Kayser–Fleischer rings, and genetic disorders in the ATP7B gene, the patient was finally diagnosed with WD

note.text: For about three years my urine has looked foamy, but I felt fine otherwise. A routine check found protein and blood in my urine, and my kidney blood test was higher than normal. A doctor noticed a very slight shaking in my hands that I had not paid attention to. A scan later showed my liver was scarred, and an eye examination found brownish rings around the edge of my corneas.
note.author: Peter's Kiro, written from the article's findings; not the patient's words
